rules.name: DCOM object activated on a remote host from PowerShell
rules.description: PowerShell creates a DCOM application object (MMC20, ShellWindows, ShellBrowserWindow, Excel) with a remote computer argument, the classic DCOM lateral movement primitive.
rules.technique_name: Remote Services: Distributed Component Object Model

rules.name: PowerShell remoting to a remote computer
rules.description: Invoke-Command or Enter-PSSession targets another computer over WinRM. Routine for administrators, so informational.

rules.name: winrs remote command execution
rules.description: winrs.exe runs a command on a remote host through WinRM, used for lateral movement.

rules.name: DNS TXT query with a long hex label
rules.description: A TXT lookup whose first label is a long hex string, the encoding DNS exfiltration tools use for chunks of data.
rules.technique_name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol: Unencrypted Non-C2 Protocol

rules.name: node -e spawning a shell fetch
rules.description: Node.js runs inline code that uses child_process to call a shell, curl or wget, a scripted download-and-run.

rules.name: Windows Script Host runs a JScript file from a user-writable path
rules.description: wscript or cscript runs a .js, .jse or .wsf file from Temp, AppData, Downloads or Public, the usual loader delivery path.

rules.name: Copy or archive into a hidden directory under a temp path
rules.description: cp, mv, rsync or tar writes into a dot-directory in /tmp, /var/tmp or /dev/shm, a common place to collect data before exfiltration.

rules.name: systeminfo or WMIC OS inventory
rules.description: systeminfo.exe, wmic os get or Get-ComputerInfo collects host and OS details; routine for administrators.

rules.name: find over the whole disk for credential or document files
rules.description: find starts at / or a home root and looks for key, password-store or document extensions.

rules.name: socat relay or shell to a remote address
rules.description: socat listens and forwards to a non-loopback peer, or binds a shell with EXEC, a network relay not tied to a standard application protocol.

rules.name: TXT lookup for a paste or raw-content host
rules.description: A TXT query for a paste or raw-hosting domain, a dead-drop resolver pattern where malware reads instructions from public services.

rules.name: Clipboard read through a command-line tool
rules.description: pbpaste, xclip -o, xsel -o or Get-Clipboard reads the clipboard; common in developer scripts, so informational.

rules.name: SMB share enumeration
rules.description: smbclient -L, net view, showmount -e or smbmap lists shares on a remote host; used by administrators and attackers alike.

rules.name: Desktop wallpaper image replaced
rules.description: The cached wallpaper file changed, which also happens when a user sets a new background; combined with other events it can indicate defacement.

rules.name: Virtualisation fingerprint commands
rules.description: Commands that read hypervisor flags or hardware vendor strings, used by malware to decide whether it runs in a sandbox.

rules.name: hping3 or nping flood
rules.description: hping3 in flood mode or nping with a high rate, the usual single-host packet flood tooling.

rules.name: Security product inventory through SecurityCenter2
rules.description: WMIC or PowerShell queries the SecurityCenter2 namespace for antivirus, antispyware or firewall products, a way to find the defences to evade.

rules.name: Immediate shutdown or poweroff
rules.description: shutdown -h now, poweroff, halt or shutdown /s /t 0; routine maintenance, but also the way an attacker stops a system.

rules.name: WMI permanent event subscription created
rules.description: A WMI event filter, consumer or binding is created in the root\subscription namespace, a fileless persistence mechanism.
rules.technique_name: Event Triggered Execution: WMI Event Subscription

rules.name: Registry hijack of a UAC auto-elevate handler
rules.description: A per-user shell-open command is written under ms-settings, mscfile or exefile classes, the registry change behind fodhelper, eventvwr and computerdefaults UAC bypasses.
rules.technique_name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Bypass User Account Control

rules.name: Shell history of another account read
rules.description: A command reads a shell or database history file under /root or another user's home, where passwords often sit in command lines.

rules.name: Browser credential database copied
rules.description: A command copies or reads the Login Data, logins.json or key4.db browser credential stores.
rules.technique_name: Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers

rules.name: Hidden directory created under a temp path
rules.description: mkdir creates a dot-directory below /tmp, /var/tmp or /dev/shm, where droppers hide payloads from casual listing.
rules.technique_name: Hide Artifacts: Hidden Files and Directories

rules.name: File created inside a hidden directory under a temp path
rules.description: A file appears in a dot-directory below /tmp, /var/tmp or /dev/shm.
rules.technique_name: Hide Artifacts: Hidden Files and Directories

rules.name: Consonant-only long label on a low-reputation TLD
rules.description: A name whose first label is ten or more characters with no vowels under a TLD popular with throwaway domains, typical of domain-generation algorithms.

rules.name: Cloud CLI infrastructure listing
rules.description: aws, gcloud or az lists instances, buckets, security groups or accounts; routine for operators, informational.

rules.name: kubectl listing pods across all namespaces
rules.description: kubectl get pods with -A or --all-namespaces; routine for operators, informational.

rules.name: Cloud-managed remote command execution
rules.description: aws ssm send-command with a shell document, az vm run-command invoke, or gcloud compute ssh --command runs code on instances through the cloud control plane.

positive.command: aws ssm send-command --instance-ids i-0abc --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --parameters commands=id

rules.name: ssh with a key from a temp path and host-key checks off
rules.description: ssh authenticates with a key stored in a temp or hidden path while disabling host-key verification, the pattern of scripted lateral movement.

rules.name: curl uploading a file to a raw public IP
rules.description: curl -T, --upload-file, --data-binary @file or -F file=@ sends a local file to an address given as a public IPv4 literal.

rules.name: gdb attached to a process to call dlopen
rules.description: gdb attaches to a running process by pid and calls dlopen or mmap, ptrace-based shared-object injection.

rules.name: DNS tunnelling tool executed
rules.description: iodine, dnscat2, dns2tcp or similar tooling that carries traffic inside DNS queries.

rules.name: ssh SOCKS proxy to a raw public IP
rules.description: ssh -D opens a dynamic SOCKS proxy with no remote command towards a public IPv4 literal, turning the host into a proxy.

rules.name: Web server process spawns a shell running recon commands
rules.description: A web server or application-server parent starts a shell that runs id, whoami, uname or reads /etc/passwd, typical right after remote code execution through an exposed application.

rules.name: Package install script fetching and piping to a shell
rules.description: A package manager parent runs a command that downloads with curl or wget and pipes to a shell, the install-script pattern used in supply chain compromises.
rules.technique_name: Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain

rules.name: Hidden PowerShell download-and-execute launched from the Run dialog
rules.description: explorer starts PowerShell with a hidden window and an iex of a downloaded string, the command victims paste in ClickFix lures.
rules.technique_name: User Execution: Malicious Copy and Paste

rules.name: Recursive delete of several data or backup directories
rules.description: rm -rf names at least two database, backup or service-data roots in one command.

rules.name: rm with --no-preserve-root
rules.description: rm is invoked with --no-preserve-root, which only makes sense for deleting the filesystem root.

rules.name: Cloud snapshot or image permission granted to another account
rules.description: aws ec2 modify-snapshot-attribute or modify-image-attribute adding accounts or the all group, or the RDS snapshot equivalent, moves data to an outside account.

positive.command: aws ec2 modify-snapshot-attribute --snapshot-id snap-0abc --attribute createVolumePermission --operation-type add --user-ids 123456789012

rules.name: LaunchAgent property list created
rules.description: A plist appears in a LaunchAgents directory; installers do this routinely, so it is informational and useful in chains.
rules.technique_name: Create or Modify System Process: Launch Agent

rules.name: Shell startup file appended with a launcher
rules.description: A command appends to .bashrc, .zshrc, .profile or similar a line that starts a background job from a temp path, downloads code or opens a reverse shell.
rules.technique_name: Event Triggered Execution: Unix Shell Configuration Modification

rules.name: Pass-the-hash arguments on a command line
rules.description: A command line supplies an NTLM hash directly to a tool: mimikatz sekurlsa::pth, impacket -hashes, pth-* utilities or /ntlm:.
rules.technique_name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Hash

rules.name: Office application spawns a command or script interpreter
rules.description: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook or OneNote starts cmd, PowerShell, a script host or a proxy-execution binary, the post-click step of a malicious attachment.

rules.name: Command executed inside a container
rules.description: docker, podman, nerdctl or kubectl exec runs a command in a running container; routine for operators, informational.

rules.name: Detached privileged or host-namespace container started
rules.description: docker or podman run -d with --privileged or --pid=host starts a long-lived container with host-level reach.

rules.name: Inline interpreter code using memfd_create
rules.description: python, perl or ruby one-liners call memfd_create (and usually fexecve), running code from an anonymous memory file with nothing on disk.
